page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7t.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals moderate single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average tier. However, multi-core scaling presents a notable bottleneck, as evidenced by weak multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores, alongside a poor multi-threaded bzip3 decompression result. Memory performance is also constrained, with both small-block cached and large-block uncached read/write bandwidth benchmarks ranking in the bottom 25%. Despite these limitations, the processor's cryptographic and vector extensions support average performance in encryption tests and static web serving throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g7t.xlarge offers a standard resource density suitable for entry-level general-purpose workloads that do not demand high memory throughput or intensive parallel processing. It is best suited for lightweight web serving, basic text processing, and small-scale application hosting. It is less optimal for database operations, software compilation, or memory-bound tasks due to its lower-tier memory bandwidth and multi-core performance characteristics.
